**Video:** [Tutorial 15 Part 2 — Deep RNNs, LSTMs and GRUs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nJivfX9VY7Y)

## Learning goals

- Stack recurrent layers so layer $\ell$ reads the sequence of hiddens from layer $\ell-1$.
- Use **bidirectional** RNNs when the whole sequence is available offline.
- Apply depth practically: dropout between layers, gradient clipping, sensible widths.

## Before this clicks

A single recurrent layer mixes time; **depth** mixes features at each time. A deep RNN is not “more time steps” — it is several recurrent modules stacked so $h_t^{(\ell)}$ depends on $h_t^{(\ell-1)}$ and $h_{t-1}^{(\ell)}$. Bidirectional models run a forward and a backward recurrent net and concatenate states when future context is allowed (not for strict causal generation).

---

## Main ideas

### 1. Stacked (deep) recurrence

For layer $\ell=1,\ldots,L$:

$$
h_t^{(\ell)}=\mathrm{RNN}^{(\ell)}\!\bigl(h_t^{(\ell-1)},\,h_{t-1}^{(\ell)}\bigr),
$$

with $h_t^{(0)}:=x_t$. Each layer has its own weights. Top layer $h_t^{(L)}$ feeds the task head.

Same stacking works with LSTM or GRU cells instead of vanilla RNN cells.

### 2. Why go deep?

Lower layers capture short / local patterns; higher layers compose them (analogous to deep CNNs). Empirically, 2–3 recurrent layers often help; extreme depth needs residuals or careful init.

### 3. Bidirectional RNNs

Forward state $\overrightarrow{h}_t$ sees $x_1,\ldots,x_t$; backward $\overleftarrow{h}_t$ sees $x_T,\ldots,x_t$. Representation:

$$
h_t=\bigl[\overrightarrow{h}_t;\,\overleftarrow{h}_t\bigr].
$$

Use for labeling, classification of full utterances, offline ASR/NLP — **not** when you must predict the next token online without peeking ahead.

### 4. Regularization and training tips

| Knob | Role |
|------|------|
| Dropout between layers / on inputs | Reduce co-adaptation |
| Gradient clipping | Tame exploding norms |
| Layer sizes decreasing or constant | Capacity vs compute |
| Pack padded sequences | Correct batching of variable $T$ |

Deep stacks amplify vanishing issues; prefer LSTM/GRU units when $T$ or $L$ grows.

### 5. Deep + bidirectional

Common pattern: 2 bidirectional LSTM layers, then a dense CRF/softmax head for sequence tagging. Output at each $t$ uses both past and future context from every layer.

---

## Worked mini-example

Sentence of length $T=4$, embedding size $4$, two stacked GRUs with hidden size $8$, then bidirectional on the top layer only.

- Layer 1: map $x_t\in\mathbb{R}^{4}\to h_t^{(1)}\in\mathbb{R}^{8}$ over time.
- Layer 2 biGRU: forward and backward each output $\mathbb{R}^{8}$ $\Rightarrow$ $h_t\in\mathbb{R}^{16}$.
- Token classifier: $W\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times 16}$ times $h_t$.

Parameter count grows with $L$ and direction, not with $T$ (aside from compute). Batching still uses `(batch, time, dim)` with masks.

---

## Common confusions

| Confusion | Clarification |
|-----------|---------------|
| Deep RNN = longer BPTT | Depth is vertical stacking; BPTT length is the time unroll |
| Bidirectional always better | Illegal for causal next-step prediction |
| More layers always help | Diminishing returns + harder optimization |
| Vanilla deep RNN is fine for long $T$ | Prefer gated cells when depth or length is large |
